confidence_rationale: Canonical documentation that pure curiosity is reward-agnostic (noisy-TV) and succeeds only where environment design aligns novelty with reward; directly explains why REE's ICM arm failed and why the whole novelty class plateaus. Weakens 'build more curiosity'.
failure_signatures: A purely curious agent that finds a stochastic/unpredictable source (a noisy TV) parks in front of it forever, because prediction error stays permanently high -- the noisy-TV problem.
Forward-model prediction-error curiosity (ICM) is the most noisy-TV-vulnerable member of the class; REE's ac_zworld_icm arm reproduced this (0.22, sub-floor).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across 54 environments, purely curiosity-driven agents (forward-model prediction error, no extrinsic reward) play many Atari games competently BECAUSE game designers align extrinsic reward with novelty; where that alignment breaks (stochastic elements) curiosity fails (noisy-TV).
mapping.ree_translation: Explains REE's V3-EXQ-751 result that ICM (forward-model curiosity) did NOT clear the floor (0.22) despite higher intrinsic reward than RND -- the forward model is the most noisy-TV-prone variant, and the forager only weakly aligns novelty with reward.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The study runs pure-curiosity (no extrinsic reward); REE trains with sparse extrinsic reward + bonus, so the noisy-TV pathology is milder, but the reward-agnostic-coverage conclusion still bounds what the class can deliver.
mapping.source_context: Deep RL over 54 environments incl. full Atari, pixel observations, feature-space ablations.

confidence_components.notes: Diagnostic value is high; it tells us the plateau is the class's expected behaviour, not a tuning failure.
